question: A gas company needs to monitor its production processes. Each production process has a process ID, name, start time, end time, and operator ID. Operators have operator ID, name, department, and contact information. Each monitoring record includes recording time, monitoring parameters, production process ID, and operator ID.
ddl:
-- Schema for database: rschema_0289

CREATE TABLE `production_processes` (
  `process_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `start_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `end_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `operator_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`process_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`operator_id`) REFERENCES `operators` (`operator_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `operators` (
  `operator_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `department` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `contact_information` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`operator_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `monitoring_records` (
  `recording_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `monitoring_parameters` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `process_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `operator_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`recording_time`, `process_id`, `operator_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`process_id`) REFERENCES `production_processes` (`process_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`operator_id`) REFERENCES `operators` (`operator_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
